title: 3.6.4 Lab: Predict Output — Primitive vs. Array Argument
description: Write one function that reassigns a number parameter and one that mutates an array parameter, then log the caller's variables to prove which change escaped. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write a function that reassigns a number parameter
steps.instructions: Define a function called changeNum that takes one parameter and reassigns it to a different number inside the body. This models a primitive argument arriving as a copy.

steps.title: Write a function that mutates an array parameter
steps.instructions: Define a second function called changeArr that takes one parameter and adds an item to it with .push. This models an array argument arriving as a copy of a reference.

steps.title: Call both and log the caller's variables
steps.instructions: Create a number variable and an array variable in the main program. Pass each to its function, then console.log both caller variables afterwards. Predict first: the number is unchanged, the array is not.

requirements.title: changeNum defined
requirements.description: Code defines a function named changeNum. Help: 3.6.2 (Pass by Value vs Reference)
requirements.hint: Define a function called changeNum with one parameter and assign that parameter a different number inside.

requirements.title: changeArr defined
requirements.description: Code defines a function named changeArr. Help: 3.6.2 (Pass by Value vs Reference)
requirements.hint: Define a function called changeArr with one parameter. Inside it, add an item to that parameter.

requirements.title: .push used
requirements.description: Code calls .push on the array parameter. Help: 3.3.2 (Array Basics: Index, push, pop)
requirements.hint: Use .push on the array parameter. This changes the one array the caller also holds.

requirements.title: caller variables logged
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.6.2 (Pass by Value vs Reference)
requirements.hint: Log the number and the array in the main program, after both calls, then compare with your prediction.

requirements.title: changeArr adds to the array it is given, and both caller variables are printed
requirements.description: changeArr([1, 2]) leaves that same array as [1, 2, <one more item>], and at least two lines are printed. Help: 3.6.3 (Example: Mutating an Array Parameter)
requirements.hint: changeArr must call .push on the parameter itself. Then print the number and the array, in that order, after both calls.

checks.expr: typeof changeNum === 'function' && typeof changeArr === 'function' && (a => { changeArr(a); return a.length === 3 && a[0] === 1 && a[1] === 2; })([1, 2]) && output.length >= 2
checks.fail: changeArr should add one item to the array it receives, so changeArr([1, 2]) leaves [1, 2, something]. Print the number and the array after calling both functions.
